description: Minimal capability set. The framework's own grants come first: `core:default` is Tauri's baseline — the IPC channel this app's commands travel over, plus window and webview basics — and `core:event:default` is the event bus every `agent:*` and `pty:*` stream is delivered on, so a session's output could not reach the webview without it. Both are `*:default` and are the only two permitted to be, because they are Tauri's rather than a plugin's: their contents move only with the framework version already pinned in Cargo.lock. Beyond those, two individual window permissions: `core:window:allow-set-theme`, because the app paints its own light/dark palettes and the native window chrome has to follow them, and `core:window:allow-start-dragging`, because the title bar is drawn by this app rather than by the OS and a custom title bar that cannot move the window is not one. With one exception the frontend reaches the outside world only through this app's own #[tauri::command] functions, so no filesystem, shell or HTTP plugin permissions are granted — every side effect goes through Rust code that enforces timeouts, PATH resolution and config trust. The exception is `dialog:allow-open`, which backs two pickers: the Browse… button in Add a repository, and the + button in an agent composer. Both show an OS picker and return only the paths the user chose in it — no directory listing, no file read, and no access to anything not explicitly selected. A repository path is then validated by the same `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` a typed path goes through, and a composer path is only ever inserted into the message box as text for the user to review before sending. So this is a convenience over typing a path rather than a way around the checks on one. `dialog:default` is deliberately not used, because it would also grant save dialogs and the native message/ask/confirm prompts, none of which this app has any use for. Notifications used to be a second exception with three `notification:allow-*` grants, and are now none at all: posting goes through this app's own `post_notification` command, because a notification now carries a navigation payload its click delivers back (see `notifier.rs` and `wtm-notify`), and the permission calls go through commands for the same reason. The notification plugin is still a Rust-side dependency — the posting fallback where the native center does not exist — but the webview can no longer address it, which is a strictly smaller grant surface than before. `core:window:allow-set-badge-count` is the dock count of sessions waiting on an answer; it is listed here because it is not part of `core:window:default`, which is also why `allow-set-theme` appears beside it. Note two things that need no permission at all: file drag-and-drop onto the composer rides `core:event:default` via the window's own `tauri://drag-drop` event, which is why `dragDropEnabled` is true in tauri.conf.json; and detecting whether the window is in front uses the DOM's own focus and blur events, the same ones the app's refresh policy already runs on, rather than a window API.
